summaryZh: Carlin 实验室研究决定宿主与病原体相互作用结局的转录调控机制，关注病毒如何削弱抗病毒免疫、抗病毒转录网络的细胞类型差异，以及 Siglec 受体和人群遗传差异如何影响病原识别与易感性。
researchQuestions: 病毒如何改变细胞调控机制并削弱抗病毒防御？
炎症转录因子与细胞类型特异的调控因子如何启动抗病毒基因程序？
病原体与 Siglec 的相互作用及其人群遗传差异如何影响感染易感性？
topics: 宿主与病原体相互作用的转录调控
病毒免疫逃逸与抗病毒转录网络
Siglec 识别与感染易感性
系统层次的宿主与病毒数据分析
methods: 转录组学与表观基因组学
NGS 数据整合与测序协议开发

evidence.quote: Welcome to the Carlin Laboratory Virology | Genomics | Systems Biology The Carlin Lab is located at the UCSD School of Medicine, in La Jolla, CA.
Dr. Carlin's lab investigates transcriptional mechanisms that determine the outcome of host-pathogen interactions.

We are very interested in how viruses influence regulatory mechanisms to subvert cellular defenses. This includes effects that are gene-specific, transcription factor specific as well as global effects on transcription, splicing, and RNA stability. We aim to determine if specific interactions occur universally or in a cell-type specific manner and how they contribute to virulence.

We study how the interplay between key inflammatory transcription factors, such as IRFs, NF-kB, and STATs, and cell-type specific master regulators (e.g. PU.1, C/EBP) induce specific target genes and antiviral transcriptional programs.
We are interested in understanding how pathogen interactions with Siglecs modulate disease pathogenesis as well as how human genetic diversity of Siglecs alters susceptibility to microorganisms.
Complementary, genome-wide methods, including CRISPR, transcriptomics and epigenomics, provide an unbiased and comprehensive way of expanding our understanding of host–viral interactions.

We study innate immune responses, leveraging genome-wide technologies and bioinformatics analysis to better understand transcriptional networks regulated by interferon regulatory factors (IRFs) and anti-viral pathways.

We are developing experimental and computational tools that improve sample processing and data integration to provide biologically meaningful conclusions. We work closely with the Heinz, Benner and Glass Laboratories at UCSD to develop optimized or innovative NGS protocols to more specifically interrogate host-viral interactions in humans.
